subject: Post-demo action items — AcroSoft model concerns & proposed safeguard
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah O'Neal <sarah.oneal@acrosoft.com>, Infra Team <infra@acrosoft.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo action items — AcroSoft model concerns & proposed safeguard

Hi Sarah / Acro infra team — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we're all aligned:

Summary from the demo:
- Use case: invoice-parsing + vendor-disambiguation for international PO ingestion (high precision required, low tolerance for hallucinations).
- Observed issue: your sampling during the live demo showed a ~9% increase in hallucination-style fillers compared to the benchmark we ran last month. You noted this seemed correlated with the platform update on Sep 29.

Proposed immediate safeguards (what we can do today):
1) Emergency pin: serve traffic from redwood-opt-7b-llm-v2 (pre-9/29 variant) while we triage v3. This is a fast revert that preserves your current production semantics.
2) Canary + comparison eval: run a 5% canary to the v3 variant with our prompt set and the attached bench (acro_bench_fails.csv) to collect diffs and concrete failure examples.
3) Short-term model recommendation: for high-precision fields, we suggest using redwood-ft-3b-qa for extraction tasks and redwood-opt-7b-llm-v2 for the orchestration/clarification layer.

Attachments I've included: acro_bench_fails.csv (sample failures from your logs), acro_prompt_set_v1.txt (the prompt templates we'll use for diffing).

Ask from you: can your infra team approve the temporary pin today? If yes, we'll open an internal rollback ticket (INF-5321) and kick off the canary evaluation. If procurement needs anything for a short-term change order, loop Lauren and Monica — they can advise on timing.

Next steps I will take if I get approval:
- Open rollback ticket and schedule a 30-min ops window this week.
- Laura will prepare the pinning playbook and runbook.
- Monica will assemble a focused eval pack that includes the failing examples you shared.

Thanks — we want to keep your service consistent while we isolate whether this is a model-regression or config-side regression.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: acro_bench_fails.csv (csv)
Attachment: acro_prompt_set_v1.txt (txt)

From: Sarah O'Neal <sarah.oneal@acrosoft.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Team <infra@acrosoft.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 11:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo action items — AcroSoft model concerns & proposed safeguard

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications and additional context from our side:

What we saw:
- After the platform update (we believe to redwood-opt-7b-llm-v3) on 2027-09-29 02:14 UTC, the QA pass for address normalization started producing plausible-but-wrong results (e.g., mapped a vendor address to another vendor in the same city). Errors are subtle and often escape current unit tests.
- We attached a short log excerpt (not full logs for privacy) that shows 7 representative failures — two are in the attached acro_bench_fails.csv.

Timeline constraints:
- Procurement needs the service stable by Oct 12 to meet our internal go-live. Any rollback or pin must not interfere with our remaining integration tests on Oct 8–10.

Immediate ask:
- Yes, please proceed with the emergency pin to v2 if that's low risk. Our infra team can approve a 30-min maintenance window after 18:00 PDT this week (Oct 5–7).

Follow-ups I need from Redwood:
- A short doc that lists the concrete diffs you expect to see in the canary (e.g., token-level hallucination metrics, example-level precision drop), with thresholds that would trigger a full rollback.
- A timeline estimate for root-cause triage (is this likely model-weight drift vs tokenization/config change?).

I'll loop procurement on the CC if we need a formal change order. Thanks again for moving fast here — this is a hard-stop for our go-live if unresolved.

—Sarah O'Neal
Head of Integrations, AcroSoft
sarah.oneal@acrosoft.com
Attachment: acro_bench_fails.csv (csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sarah O'Neal <sarah.oneal@acrosoft.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 15:30:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo action items — AcroSoft model concerns & proposed safeguard

On Mon, Oct 4, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sarah / Acro infra team — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we're all aligned:

Thanks Marcus — this is actionable. TL;DR: we can do the emergency pin today and run a controlled canary. Details below and a runbook attached.

Immediate technical plan (short version):
1) Emergency pin: set model alias acro-prod-inference -> redwood-opt-7b-llm-v2. This operation is reversible and will keep existing weights/kv cache layout intact. Expected propagation: ~4–8 minutes to edge pools.
2) Canary: route 5% traffic for 24 hours to redwood-opt-7b-llm-v3 (instrumented). We'll collect the following metrics per request: token hallucination score (our internal heuristic), top-k token disagreement, and example-level precision/recall relative to the eval set.
3) Thresholds to trigger rollback: >3% absolute degradation in example-level precision OR >0.05 increase in median token-hallucination score across the canary set. These are conservative thresholds given the risk profile Sarah described.

Operational notes:
- Maintenance window: prefer Oct 5, 18:00–18:30 PDT. Marcus / Acro infra to confirm.
- If pin approved, I will open INF-5321 and attach pin_instructions.md which contains step-by-step commands and rollback commands.
- Monica: can you start assembling an eval pack that includes the 7 representative failures from the attachment plus 200 random production samples (strip PII)? Please upload to the Drive folder linked.

I'll attach pin_instructions.md and the short canary checklist. If Acro needs a deeper forensics run, our applied ML team can ingest the failing examples and run a token-level trace.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Attachment: pin_instructions.md (md)
Attachment: canary_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo action items — AcroSoft model concerns & proposed safeguard

Thanks Sarah — confirming next steps and owners.

Action items (I opened INF-5321):
- Laura: run the emergency pin during Oct 5, 18:00–18:30 PDT maintenance window and start the 24h 5% canary.
- Monica: assemble eval pack and upload to Drive by EOD Oct 5 (include acro_prompt_set_v1.txt + 200 anonymized samples).
- Lauren: help procurement craft a short change request if Acro needs it for Oct 12 go-live.

I will join the post-canary review and coordinate with Sarah on whether the thresholds are met to proceed with a full rollback. We'll aim to have initial canary metrics within 26 hours of the pin.

If anything changes from Acro infra (timing or additional failing examples), please notify us immediately.
